newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA political arm warns of more attacks in Spain.
newsitem.headline: ETA political arm warns of more attacks in Spain.

text.p: The leader of the political arm of the violent Basque separatist group ETA issued a veiled warning on Wednesday that Spain's arrests of its leaders could lead to further ETA attacks.

"It (arrest and subsequent jailings) could bring costs to this society," Herri Batasuna leader Jon Idigoras told a news conference in the northern Basque city of San Sebastian. "The actual consequences will not be desired."

A Basque politician, HB leader Itziar Aizpurua, was arrested on Tuesday for failing to appear in the Supreme Court to answer charges the party used a video to promote ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) violence.
Two other HB politicians were arrested on Monday and held after refusing to post five million pesetas ($37,000) bail.
ETA has killed some 800 people since starting a drive for Basque independence in 1968.

The Supreme Court has summoned all 25 members of HB's leadership on charges they edited and distributed an ETA video during a general election last March and made statements justifying two ETA assassinations.
The HB leaders, who do not disavow violence as a means to achieve Basque independence, have been called to testify from February 3-18, but have said they would not appear.
"We refuse to appear," HB leader Tasio Erkizia said on Monday. "Spanish courts are foreign, far removed from the Basque people."
